# Text & fonts

## Script

### Every word not working works against you
<a id="text-kaplans-law"></a>

Kaplan's Law of Words; pull-out test: if a sentence can be removed and the paragraph still works, cut it; a paragraph is a burrito that shouldn't come apart in the air.

> any words that aren't working for you are working against you.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L09](../sources/L09.md)

Related: ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile)

### Visualize, falsify, nobody else can say it
<a id="text-three-rules"></a>

Run every line through three questions: can I visualize it, can I falsify it, can nobody else say it? Three no's = rubbish; three yes's = onto something.

> Can I visualize it? Can I falsify it? Can nobody else say this?

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L09](../sources/L09.md)

Related: [Point, don't talk; give me a fact](../topics/text.md#text-point-dont-talk), [Even "here's three things" beats no frame](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-any-framework-beats-none), [Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete), [Structure = dividing lines + parallelism](../topics/story.md#story-dividing-lines-parallelism)

### Make it concrete and visual
<a id="text-zoom-in-concrete"></a>

Rewrite down an abstract → concrete ladder until you hit an object (regain fitness → Couch to 5K) and swap literal words for visual ones ("1,000 songs in your pocket", not "media player").

> If you can't visualize it, you won't remember it.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L09](../sources/L09.md)

### Point, don't talk; give me a fact
<a id="text-point-dont-talk"></a>

Swap adjectives for pointable facts ("Looks like Ryan Gosling, 6'2"" beats "smart, funny"). If in doubt, give a fact, then build on it (Heinz bottles refilled → "Even when it's not Heinz, it's Heinz").

> This takes work. That's why it's better.

<a id="text-compare-to-known"></a>

### Copy devices: time frames, reframes, alliteration
<a id="text-expand-time-frame"></a>

Expand the time frame (22,000 career hours vs 4 a day), reframe a cost as a saving, tweak numbers for parallelism (22,000 / 2), and pair alliteration with a contradiction ("The dating app designed to be deleted").

## Edit

### Plain shadowed captions, no box
<a id="l10-plain-shadow-captions"></a>

Captions as plain white bold sans (SF Pro/Inter-like) with a soft drop shadow and no background box, 1-3 words, centred at ~61% height just above the laptop edge. He calls it cleaner than the source's green box.

**How:** CapCut: Text > white bold sans, Shadow on (soft, ~40% opacity), no background; auto-captions split to 1-3 words.

> I'd lose the green box though. Plain text with shadow looks way cleaner.

<a id="l10-prompt-bar-on-screen"></a>

### Tool card lands on the word
<a id="l10-card-on-the-word"></a>

GitHub repo cards (openai/whisper, yt-dlp) and logo cards (FFmpeg) appear exactly when the tool is named, timed from Whisper word timestamps. The caption: captions, tool labels and repo cards "land exactly when I say them".

**How:** Get word timings (faster-whisper), then start each card on the first frame of its word, with a pop.

> Whisper gets the timing of every word, so captions, tool labels and GitHub repo cards land exactly when I say them.

<a id="l11-template-card-typography"></a>

<a id="text-two-line-paragraphs"></a>

> short paragraphs are like monkey bars. They're easy to swing between
